claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulation can be used to study the size-dependent thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Decreasing FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticle size diminishes thermal stability.
Decreasing FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticle size lowers the effective melting temperature.
The proposed nanoparticles have a homogeneous elemental distribution in their as-synthesized state.
The nanoparticles will be heated at controlled rates in MD simulations across a range of particle sizes.
The simulations will use ambient-pressure, canonical-ensemble (NVT) conditions.
Smaller nanoparticles have a larger surface-to-volume ratio.
A larger surface-to-volume ratio increases surface-atom activity.
Surface atoms in smaller nanoparticles have lower coordination numbers.
Lower surface-atom coordination weakens interatomic binding.
Weaker interatomic binding promotes an earlier onset of atomic mobility and melting during heating.
Nanoparticles below a critical diameter will have significantly lower melting temperatures than larger nanoparticles and bulk FeCuCrCoNi.
Reduced thermal stability will be observable as earlier structural degradation and melting in MD simulations.
Surface effects are minimal in bulk FeCuCrCoNi relative to nanoparticles.
Atomic displacement, radial distribution functions, and coordination-number distributions can identify surface melting and structural disorder.
